VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed answer $q^n$ is not correct in general. The complement of a hyperplane gives a valid codeword of weight $q^n$, but it is not always minimal. For even $q$, $d(2,q)=q+2$ (a hyperoval), and $q^{n-2}d(2,q)=q^{n-2}(q+2)$ is smaller than $q^n$ whenever $q>2$. The expected form is $d(n,q)=q^{n-2}\,d(2,q)$, which agrees with $q^n$ when $q$ is odd, where $d(2,q)=q^2$.

I did not verify the lifting argument from a plane codeword to a codeword in $\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$ in full detail. The conclusion depends on that construction existing, so my confidence is moderate.

CONFIDENCE: 4
